note: Standard CsCl lattice parameter (a=4.123 Angstrom); Cs-Cl nearest-neighbor distance = a*sqrt(3)/2 = 3.5706 Angstrom, a published reference value. Reserved: not used to design or tune B1's cell-list neighbor search -- checked only after the implementation is frozen, per this project's established holdout discipline, to confirm the new algorithm's exact minimum-image guarantee generalizes to a simple-cubic two-species case it was not built against.

Standard HCP magnesium lattice parameters (a=3.2094, c=5.2108 Angstrom, c/a=1.6236, close to the ideal 1.633). A non-orthogonal (gamma=120 degree) but non-triclinic case -- distinct stress shape from mat-01's fully-triclinic fixture and mat-06's near-degenerate rhombohedral fixture. Reserved the same way as mat-holdout-01: not used to shape B1's design, checked only afterward.

Not a new structure -- reserved as a specific, large-N performance-scaling check for B1's neighbor-search rewrite, deliberately sized well beyond the toy-scale fixtures used to design correctness (mat-01 through mat-06 are all under 10 sites). This is where the O(n^2) to cell-list improvement should become measurable; reserved so the performance claim in a future B1 implementation PR is checked against a case chosen now, not cherry-picked after the fact to make the speedup look good.

Combines two individually-tested-elsewhere properties (triclinic lattice, mat-01; partial occupancy, mat-04) that have never been tested together in this fixture set. Reserved specifically because combined-property interactions are a common source of bugs this project's own history has caught before (e.g. the tie-break regression fixture in periodic.rs was found via exactly this kind of combined-case triclinic testing) -- checked only after B1/B2's design is frozen against the individually-simpler fixtures.
